input: A skill's "## logging" section keeps drifting to an unanchored path (bare logs/usage.jsonl). An agent should be able to run one command on a file or a directory of files, on demand, after editing a skill, to catch this before it ships.
expect: picks a checker (agent invokes it deliberately, on files already in front of it); tools/<name>/ with Cargo.toml + src/main.rs, inline #[cfg(test)] tests, cargo fmt/clippy/test all named, exit code carries the verdict, no registration step needed

input: Every time an agent writes to a path under ~/.pi or ~/.agents directly instead of editing the source and running install.sh, it silently desyncs the managed config from the repo. This must never happen even if the agent forgets to check first.
expect: picks a Pi extension (must not depend on an agent remembering to run it) hooking pi.on("tool_call") for edit/write/bash, returning {block:true, reason} before the write executes; names config/tools.toml registration; points to config-write-guard as the existing precedent to extend rather than duplicate since it already covers this exact case

input: After Git creates or switches a worktree branch, checkout must stay lightweight: start no compiler or sandbox build, and never copy files between checkouts or alter checked-out content. Complete sandbox builds must remain explicit operations separate from Git's checkout event.
expect: picks the existing post-checkout git hook as the behavior to correct rather than adding another hook or tool; removes any compiler or sandbox-build launch from checkout; keeps a header naming the Git event and stating that the hook must never start a compiler or sandbox build, copy files between worktrees, or change checked-out content; keeps complete sandbox builds available only as explicit, separate commands outside the checkout hook; names a scratch-repository PASS/FAIL test script that proves checkout starts no build and preserves checkout content

input: A skill keeps producing PR descriptions with inconsistent tone — sometimes too casual, sometimes too formal — and the user wants something to catch and reject a bad-tone PR body before it ships.
expect: declines to build a hard-gate checker for tone; states that tone is a judgment call (ai-author's decidable-vs-right test) and a checker here would carry false authority; either proposes it as a review signal only (never a blocking gate) or routes to the byline/mouthpiece skill as the actual owner of tone, not a new tools/ or pi/extensions/ artifact

input: A new Pi extension needs to block a specific class of Bash command (writes to a path outside the repo) before it runs, and the actual path-outside-repo check is genuine computation: resolving symlinks, canonicalizing relative paths, and comparing against the repo root.
expect: picks a Pi extension, but recommends the Rust-shell-out shape (tools/<name>/ checker doing the canonicalization + comparison, pi.exec calling the built binary, thin TS wiring translating exit code to {block, reason}) over a pure-TypeScript policy.ts, because the logic is real computation that the repository's Rust rule reaches, not a few string comparisons

input: A calling skill will run an existing Rust checker many times. Give invocation guidance that avoids starting Cargo on every unchanged call without risking a stale binary after a build-affecting change.
expect: requires an explicit cargo build first, then direct invocation of the stable built binary for repeated unchanged calls; rejects cargo run, build-on-every-invocation wrappers, and unnecessary dynamic compilation; requires an explicit rebuild after source, manifest, lockfile, toolchain, feature, profile, target, or relevant compiler-configuration changes
